title: Figuring the Closing-Year Tax Letter Amount of an Entrance Fee Agreement
content:
**Amount stated.** The closing-year letter of an **Entrance Fee Agreement** states the plan's entrance fee medical expense percentage of the entrance fee received on the agreement's ledger in the closing year plus the plan's monthly fee medical expense percentage of the payments posted to the resident's independent living ledger in the closing year, rounded to the cent half up; the closing year's entries are those posted 1 to 12 whole months before the January issue date, that is at least 1 and fewer than 13 whole months before it.

The two shares are added together before the single rounding to the cent half up.

**Plans at 0.0.** A plan whose medical expense percentages are both 0.0 receives a closing-year letter stating 0.00, whatever else the closing year holds.

## Inputs

| Share | Entries of the closing year | Percentage |
|---|---|---|
| Entrance fee share | Deposit and balance payments on the agreement's ledger | The plan's entrance fee medical expense percentage |
| Residence fee share | Payments posted to the resident's Independent Living Residency Agreement ledger | The plan's monthly fee medical expense percentage |

## Worked figures (hypothetical, LifeCare 90% Refundable Plan percentages 21.8 and 38.5)

| Entrance fee received in the closing year | Independent living payments in the closing year | Entrance fee share | Residence fee share | Amount stated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.00 | 25200.00 | 0.00 | 9702.00 | 9702.00 |
| 41500.00 | 0.00 | 9047.00 | 0.00 | 9047.00 |

The same entries under a LifeChoice plan give 0.00.
